name: Botros methenamine–trimethoprim trial
question: How does methenamine hippurate compare with trimethoprim for culture-proven UTI recurrence in adult women?

design.population: Ninety-two women aged 18 to 99 years with at least two symptomatic, culture-positive urinary tract infections (minimum 10,000 CFU/mL) in six months or three in one year were randomized; mean age was 71.9 years, 86/92 (93.5%) were postmenopausal, and 43/92 (46.7%) used vaginal estrogen. Pregnancy, urinary tract abnormalities, acute pyelonephritis, renal insufficiency or failure, and postcoital prophylaxis were exclusion criteria.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 572–573; Table 1, p 574

verdictNote: The primary comparison found no difference; no equivalence margin was prespecified.
takeaway: In this open-label randomized trial, 12-month culture-proven UTI recurrence occurred in 28/43 analyzed women (65.1%) with methenamine hippurate and 28/43 (65.1%) with trimethoprim (P=1.00); six of 92 randomized women were excluded from analysis.

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Botros C, Lozo S, Iyer S, et al. "Methenamine hippurate compared with trimethoprim for the prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections: a randomized clinical trial." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2022;33(3):571-580. doi:10.1007/s00192-021-04849-0
reports.followUp: Culture-proven UTI recurrence by 12 months after prophylaxis initiation; treatment for six months with optional continuation

results.measure: Participants with symptomatic, culture-proven recurrence by 12 months, reported intention-to-treat analysis (86/92 randomized analyzed)
results.note: The planned comparison used a 0.05 significance level to detect a 23.8 percentage-point difference; no equivalence margin or between-group confidence interval was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 573; Results and Table 2, pp 574–575

results.measure: Participants with recurrence by 12 months, per-protocol analysis
results.note: Supportive analysis of the primary endpoint after reassignment by actual medication received; 11 participants switched groups.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table 2, pp 574–575

results.measure: Days to first recurrent UTI, reported intention-to-treat analysis; mean ± SD
results.note: Prespecified secondary outcome; no between-group confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 573; Table 2, p 575

results.measure: UTI recurrences in the year after prophylaxis initiation, reported intention-to-treat analysis; mean ± SD
results.note: Before prophylaxis, yearly means were 3.7 ± 1.5 and 4.0 ± 2.1, respectively; within-group reductions had P<0.01.

harms.label: Adverse effects and discontinuation

values.ctl: diarrhea 1/47; rash 2/47; weakness 2/47; C. difficile colitis 1/47

harms.note: 10/92 patients stopped assigned medication after an adverse effect; the nephrolithiasis episode was thought unrelated.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 575; Table 4, p 577

harms.label: Trimethoprim-resistant recurrent urine cultures
harms.note: Denominators are recurrent cultures with susceptibility data, not participants; not all cultures had antibiotic sensitivities.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 576; Table 5, p 578

delivery.label: Prophylaxis duration
delivery.value: Methenamine hippurate 1 g twice daily or trimethoprim 100 mg nightly for six months; recurrence-free participants were encouraged to discontinue, with 12-month follow-up. Mean recorded treatment duration was 272.1 ± 18.4 versus 279.5 ± 17.5 days (P=0.77).
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 572–573; Results, p 575

delivery.label: Adherence and treatment switching
delivery.note: Survey distributed to 51/92 participants (55.4%); the Morisky score comparison was P=0.44 between arms; 11/86 analyzed participants were reassigned for per-protocol analysis after switching drugs.
